chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafi, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who is moderate in his living, Allah would Grace him, and the one who squanders (wastes), Allah would Deprive him'.

key_terms.اقْتَصَدَ: To be moderate or balanced in spending/living
key_terms.مَعِيشَتِهِ: His livelihood or means of subsistence

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material consequence of being moderate versus extravagant in one's livelihood according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith links the Prophetic tradition to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting moderation (iqtidar) as a divine mechanism for sustaining livelihood. It contrasts the spiritual and material blessings of restraint with the deprivation resulting from wastefulness (buthr), reflecting the Shia emphasis on balanced living as a form of worship. This principle underscores that financial discipline is not merely economic but a reflection of one's gratitude and trust in Allah.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Sayrafi, from Ibn Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who is moderate in his living, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Grace him, and the one who squanders (wastes), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Deprive him’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ahmad ibn ‘Abd Allah has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali (al-Sayrafiy) from ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Whoever maintains moderation, Allah grants him sustenance, but He deprives one who spends excessively.’”
